question: Why did 5-fold CV without shuffling give such a low accuracy on the iris data?

answers.answer: The rows are sorted by species, so the validation folds contained species that were underrepresented in training
answers.feedback: Correct! The low accuracy is caused by the row order, not by the model.

answers.answer: 5 folds are too few for 150 observations
answers.feedback: Not quite. With shuffling, the same 5 folds give a reasonable accuracy of 0.81.
Not quite. The folds never overlap in k-fold CV, with or without shuffling.

question: You run LOOCV on a dataset with 200 observations. How many models are fitted?

answers.feedback: Correct! LOOCV fits one model per observation.
Not quite. In LOOCV, k equals the number of observations, and every fold is left out once.

question: You ran 5-fold CV and the model from fold 2 had the highest accuracy. Which model do you use to make predictions on new data?

answers.answer: A new model, fitted on the complete dataset
answers.feedback: Correct! The fold models only serve to estimate performance.
Not quite. Fold 2 probably just had an easier validation fold.

answers.answer: The average of the five fold models
answers.feedback: Not quite. The fold models are only used to estimate the performance. Each of them also saw only 80% of the data.

question: You compare 10 models and pick the one with the best score on your test set. How good is that score as an estimate of the performance on new data?

answers.feedback: Correct! Choosing the best of 10 scores favors models that got lucky on this test set. You would need a separate test set to evaluate the chosen model.
Not quite. By choosing a model based on the test set, you used it as a validation set.
Not quite. Picking the best of several scores tends to favor models that got lucky.
